newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO SET FOR "COMMANDO OPERATION" AT LENS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO SET FOR "COMMANDO OPERATION" AT LENS.

text.p: Monaco are set for a "commando operation" at Lens where they expect a hot reception on Friday after their 5-1 home rout of the same team in September precipitated the northerners' crash from top to 16th.

The French first division leaders want to retain their two-point advantage over Paris St-Germain, who play Montpellier, ahead of their top-of-the-table clash in the principality when league action resumes in January after the winter recess.

Lens, who won their first four games of the season before the defeat at Monaco, are desperate to regain their confidence after taking just one point from their last eight matches, the worst run in the first division this season.
"(This is a) commando operation, do-or-die to stay in front during the recess," Monaco coach Jean Tigana said.

Ali Benarbia, who has taken the playmaker mantle of injured Belgian international Enzo Scifo, said: "We have to be in a position of strength when we meet them (PSG). So it would be better not to lose at Lens.

"We lost there last year and they absolutely need a victory and they are going to go all out. We know about their fighting qualities, there is danger so we'll have to prepare for a tough match and we'll need a commando spirit to reply to their determination."
France under-21 midfielder Sylvain Legwinski said: "No doubt they still have the 5-1 away (result) in their throats and with the help of their fans they're going to give us a hot reception.
"It will a bit like our match at Marseille, and even if we learnt the lesson of the Velodrome we must be on our guard."

Monaco lost 3-1 away to Marseille on November 6, their last defeat and the last time they conceded a goal, when they were unsettled by the Velodrome crowd. The fervour of the Lens fans is second only to Marseille's in France.
Lens goalkeeper Guillaume Warmuz, back last weekend in the 1-0 defeat at Montpellier after an injury layoff since April, confirmed the main cause of Lens' ills.
"I don't think the team ever recovered from the 5-1 defeat at Monaco at the beginning of September. It was the turning point in the season. That 5-1 did a lot of damage," he said.
Lens picked up only three points from the next eight matches, dropping from first to 14th. Then a brief revival of three wins in a row took them back up to fourth before the current slump.
They have also lost four times at home already including their last three games at their Bollaert ground where only Guingamp picked up all three points last season.
Warmuz said: "So, the message I'm trying to get through is: let's stop doubting. At Niort (in a League Cup victory) and Montpellier we had three good halves out of four."
Lens welcome back David Regis after a two-match suspension, but lose another defender, also suspended, penalty specialist Frederic Dehu.

The Monaco squad has one change from that which won 1-0 at home to Cannes last weekend with defender Philippe Leonard returning from World Cup duty with Belgium, while midfielder Laurent Viaud has pulled out with an injury.
